_comment: Q9.6 CANARY. This fixture is DELIBERATELY CORRUPT and must never be used as
Why it exists: a leakage test that never actually exercises its assertion
passes forever and proves nothing. Q9.2 asks for a test that asserts the
behaviour-window boundary, so the test suite must also demonstrate that the
test is CAPABLE of failing. tests/test_leakage.py feeds this fixture to the
leakage checker and asserts it RAISES; if the checker ever accepts this,
the checker is broken no matter how green the other leakage tests look.
Three distinct violations, one per case, so a checker that catches only the
obvious one is still caught out:
future_click     history entry AFTER the impression it feeds.
boundary_equal   history entry EXACTLY AT the impression time. The rule is
strict (<), not <=: a click recorded at the same instant
is indistinguishable from one CAUSED by the impression,
and admitting it leaks the label into the features. This
is the case an off-by-one lets through.
cross_split      a user's feature row for a TEST impression built from a
click that happens after the test split began — legal by
per-row timestamp, illegal by split boundary.

boundary_equal.why: click_time EQUALS impression_time; the rule is strict <, not <=

cross_split.why: feature for a test-split impression derives from a click inside the test period

clean_control.why: identical shape, no violation. The checker must ACCEPT this — otherwise the canary tests would pass on a checker that simply rejects everything.
